intervals.label: Fly's Eye operating
intervals.note: Sokolsky & Thomson (arXiv:0706.1248) say the Fly's Eye detectors "were operated from 1982 to 1992"; Bertou et al. (astro-ph/0001516) also say 1982. The Fly's Eye collaboration's own final paper says 1981, which is used; the one-year start difference is unresolved.

intervals.label: HiRes prototype and MIA muon array (hybrid)
intervals.quote: During the lifetime of this hybrid experiment between Aug. 23, 1993 and May. 24, 1996

intervals.label: HiRes operating
intervals.quote: The HiRes I detector took data in monocular mode from 1997 to 2006, while HiRes II operated from 1999 to 2006.

intervals.label: detector operations ended
intervals.note: Start is the end of HiRes data taking. No source read says the detectors were removed from the site.
intervals.quote: operated on clear, moonless nights over a period of nine years (1997-2006)

name: Dugway Proving Ground (Fly's Eye and HiRes site)
notes: The site is on Army land; the sources thank the Army and the Dugway Proving Ground staff for their cooperation but name no operator other than the collaborations, so no operator is recorded.
The facility is recorded as completed because the experiments it hosted ended in 2006; no source read states that the stations were dismantled.

summary.plain: Army test range in the Utah desert where two generations of cosmic-ray fluorescence detectors, Fly's Eye and HiRes, watched the night sky for the faint light of giant air showers from 1981 to 2006.
summary.technical: Site on the U.S. Army Dugway Proving Ground, Utah (about 40 N, 113 W), of the Fly's Eye (two eyes 3.4 km apart, 1981/82-1992), the HiRes prototype with the MIA muon array (1993-1996) and HiRes (two stations 12.6 km apart, 1997-2006) air-fluorescence detectors.
